contents.text:
I'm settling on the core principle here: the engine names no product, identities and packs are the extension points, and hosts pick their combination at start-up. Next I'll note the consequences, keep the prose tight, and finish with the doc path and an offer.

I'm weighing whether to show a page, and deciding it isn't needed since the identity and pack details live on the overview page. I'll offer some choices next, and I need to end my words with the doc path before making that offer.

ADR 0027 decides that the engine names no product. Puls had grown into the core, so every product built on the engine carried it. The ADR splits the framework into three parts.

The engine is the core: the loop, sessions, usage and prices, guards, the shared contracts, and the tools every agent needs. It names no product and no country.

An identity (`IAgentIdentity`) says who an agent is: its voice, modes, roles, and which packs it uses. Puls, the demo, the coding agent and voorman are all identities.

A pack (`IAgentPack`) says what an agent can do: toolsets, providers, guides and settings. A pack never references another pack or an identity. The ADR also allows an identity's workflow code to use its own packs' public types.

Hosts choose the identities and packs at start-up, with the `IDENTITIES` and `PACKS` settings. One composition project, `LouisAgent.Composition`, knows them all. A new product is configured rather than coded, and an identity's assembly loads only if `IDENTITIES` names it. Identities and packs plug in only at start-up, so a chat's tools never change while it runs.
